sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips: gas pressure

board_events.text: The traps around the pressure derivation
In P = (1/3)(N/V) m vrms^2, m is one molecule's mass and N the molecule count; the density form sidesteps this because rho bundles Nm/V.
The 1/3 is purely the isotropy factor. If molecules move along one axis (directed beams, 1-D), drop it.
Pressure and kinetic energy scale as vrms squared, not vrms. Always square the speed factor first.
An elastic bounce reverses only the perpendicular component: the transfer is 2 m vx, not m vx.
Pressure is a statistical average, meaningful only for enormous N. A single molecule has no sensible pressure or temperature.
Pro-tip: given P and V, the total translational KE is E = (3/2)PV in one line.

segments.text: <curious>This derivation is a board favourite</curious>, so the traps cluster around its algebra. Five slips and one pro-tip.

First, do not confuse m, one molecule's mass, with the sample mass. In the kinetic equation m is a single molecule and N is the molecule count; mixing them up by a factor of N is the commonest derivation error. The density form sidesteps it, because rho already bundles N m over V.

Second, do not forget the one third, or forget where it comes from. It is purely the isotropy factor. Examiners test this by removing isotropy, so if a problem says molecules move along one axis, drop the one third.
Third, do not treat pressure as linear in speed. Pressure and kinetic energy scale as the square of the r m s speed, so always square the speed factor first.

Fourth, do not assume a wall collision transfers the whole momentum m v. An elastic bounce reverses only the perpendicular component, so the transfer is two m v x, not m v x. Halving this is a classic slip.

Fifth, remember pressure is a statistical average. It is only meaningful for a large collection; a single molecule rattling in a box delivers sharp, intermittent impulses, not a steady force, so you cannot sensibly assign it a pressure or a temperature.

And the pro-tip: if a question gives you pressure and volume, you instantly know the total translational kinetic energy, three halves pressure times volume. Reach for it whenever total kinetic energy appears; it usually turns a three-step problem into one line.
यह derivation board favourite है, तो traps इसकी algebra के आस-पास इकट्ठा होते हैं। पाँच slips और एक pro-tip।

पहला, m, एक molecule का mass, को sample mass से confuse मत कीजिए। kinetic equation में m एक single molecule है और N molecule count; इन्हें N के factor से मिलाना सबसे common derivation error है। density form इसे sidestep करता है, क्योंकि rho पहले ही N m over V को bundle कर देता है।

दूसरा, one third को मत भूलिए, या यह कहाँ से आता है यह मत भूलिए। यह विशुद्ध रूप से isotropy factor है। examiners इसे isotropy हटाकर test करते हैं, तो अगर problem कहे molecules एक axis के साथ move करते हैं, one third हटा दीजिए।
तीसरा, pressure को speed में linear मत समझिए। pressure और kinetic energy r m s speed के square के जैसे scale करते हैं, तो हमेशा speed factor को पहले square कीजिए।
चौथा, यह मत मानिए कि wall collision पूरा momentum m v transfer करता है। elastic bounce सिर्फ़ perpendicular component उलटता है, तो transfer two m v x है, m v x नहीं। इसे आधा करना एक classic slip है।

पाँचवाँ, याद रखिए pressure एक statistical average है। यह सिर्फ़ एक large collection के लिए meaningful है; एक box में खड़खड़ाता single molecule sharp, intermittent impulses देता है, steady force नहीं, तो आप उसे sensibly कोई pressure या temperature assign नहीं कर सकते।

और pro-tip: अगर question pressure और volume देता है, आपको तुरंत total translational kinetic energy पता है, three halves pressure into volume। जब भी total kinetic energy दिखे इसे उठाइए; <whisper>यह अक्सर एक three-step problem को one line में बदल देता है।</whisper>

board_events.text: Molecules do not share one speed: like a departing crowd, a few sprint, most amble, a handful dawdle.
Collisions share energy into a stable spread, the Maxwell distribution, so the three measures always line up in one order.
The high-speed tail lets fast molecules escape gravity: the low-gravity Moon lost its air; Earth keeps heavier N2, O2.
Trap: the average velocity (a vector) is zero; the average speed (a scalar) is not. These formulas are about speed.

segments.text: In sub-topic two we found pressure times volume equals two thirds of the energy, but we never said what temperature is at the molecular level. This subtopic closes that gap, with one of the most beautiful results in physics.

Temperature is simply a measure of the average kinetic energy of the molecules. A hot gas is not carrying heat like a bucket carries water; its molecules are literally moving faster. Cool the gas and they slow down. That is all temperature is.
The two panels capture it. A cool gas has slow molecules, a hot gas fast ones, and the average kinetic energy per molecule is fixed by the absolute temperature alone.

But the molecules do not all move at one speed. Picture a departing stadium crowd: a few sprint, most amble, a handful dawdle. We summarise such a spread with three averages, the most probable speed at the peak, the ordinary mean speed, and the root mean square speed that ties to kinetic energy.

Why three? Because the molecules share out their energy through countless collisions into a characteristic, stable spread of speeds, the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution. That is why the three measures differ, and they always line up in the same order.

This spread has dramatic consequences. A planet keeps a gas only if its molecules stay below escape speed, but the Maxwell tail always holds some far faster than average, and these slowly leak away. Light gases lose the race, so Earth keeps heavier nitrogen and oxygen while the low-gravity Moon holds essentially none.

And note the recurring trap. The average velocity, a vector, is zero, because molecules go equally in all directions. But the average speed, a scalar, is decidedly not zero. Speed is what all these formulas are about.

<curious>sub-topic two में हमने पाया</curious> pressure into volume बराबर energy का two thirds, पर हमने कभी नहीं कहा कि molecular level पर temperature क्या है। यह subtopic उस gap को भरता है, physics के सबसे खूबसूरत results में से एक के साथ।

temperature बस molecules की average kinetic energy का माप है। एक hot gas heat को ऐसे नहीं ढोता जैसे बाल्टी पानी ढोती है; उसके molecules सचमुच तेज़ move करते हैं। gas को cool कीजिए और वे धीमे हो जाते हैं। <excited>temperature बस इतना ही है।</excited>
दो panels इसे पकड़ लेते हैं। cool gas में slow molecules, hot gas में fast, और per molecule average kinetic energy सिर्फ़ absolute temperature से fix होती है।

पर molecules सब एक speed पर move नहीं करते। निकलती stadium crowd सोचिए: कुछ sprint करते हैं, ज़्यादातर amble करते हैं, कुछ dawdle करते हैं। ऐसे spread को हम तीन averages से summarise करते हैं, peak पर most probable speed, ordinary mean speed, और kinetic energy से जुड़ी root mean square speed।

तीन क्यों? क्योंकि molecules अपनी energy countless collisions के ज़रिए एक characteristic, stable spread of speeds में बाँटते हैं, Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution। इसीलिए तीनों measures अलग होते हैं, और हमेशा एक ही order में line up करते हैं।

इस spread के dramatic consequences हैं। एक planet एक gas तभी रखता है जब उसके molecules escape speed के नीचे रहें, पर Maxwell tail में हमेशा कुछ average से कहीं तेज़ होते हैं, और ये धीरे-धीरे leak हो जाते हैं। हल्की gases race हार जाती हैं, तो Earth heavier nitrogen और oxygen रखता है जबकि low-gravity Moon लगभग कुछ नहीं।

और recurring trap नोट कीजिए। average velocity, एक vector, zero है, क्योंकि molecules हर दिशा में equally जाते हैं। पर average speed, एक scalar, बिलकुल zero नहीं है। speed ही वह है जिसके बारे में ये सारी formulas हैं।

board_events.text: The curve is lopsided; that asymmetry makes the three measures differ, in order most-probable, average, rms.
Heating slides the peak right and flattens the curve, but the total area (molecule count) is fixed.
A heavier gas at the same T squeezes left: equal average energy forces slower speeds.
Read the curve as an area, not a height: the fraction in a speed range is the area under the curve there; total area = 1.
Oxygen at 300 K: vmp ~395, vav ~446, vrms ~484 m/s. Hydrogen runs about 4x faster.

segments.text: <curious>Let us look at the distribution itself.</curious> Plot the number of molecules against speed and a characteristic curve appears.
Here it is. The curve starts at zero, since no molecule is perfectly still, rises to a peak at the most probable speed, then falls away with a long tail stretching to very high speeds.

The curve is lopsided, a gentle rise then a long high-speed tail, and that asymmetry is exactly why the three speed-measures differ. They always line up as most probable, then average, then root mean square, smallest to largest.

Heat the gas and the whole curve responds. The peak slides to the right as molecules speed up, and the curve flattens and spreads over a wider range, but the total area, the total number of molecules, stays fixed.

Swap to a heavier gas at the same temperature and the curve squeezes leftward. Heavier molecules carry the same average kinetic energy, so they must move slower. <excited>Equal energy, unequal speeds</excited> explains a huge fraction of exam questions.

One reading rule is essential. The curve is read as an area, not a height. The fraction of molecules in any speed interval is the area under the curve there, and the height at a single speed is not itself a probability. The total area is always one.

To anchor it, oxygen at three hundred kelvin has a most probable speed near three hundred ninety five, an average near four hundred forty six, and an r m s near four hundred eighty four metres per second. The much lighter hydrogen runs about four times faster across the board.
आइए distribution को खुद देखें। molecules की संख्या को speed के against plot कीजिए और एक characteristic curve उभरती है।
यह रही। curve zero से शुरू होती है, क्योंकि कोई molecule बिलकुल still नहीं, most probable speed पर एक peak तक चढ़ती है, फिर एक long tail के साथ गिरती है जो बहुत high speeds तक फैली है।

curve lopsided है, एक gentle rise फिर एक long high-speed tail, और यही asymmetry है जिससे तीनों speed-measures अलग होते हैं। वे हमेशा most probable, फिर average, फिर root mean square, छोटे से बड़े क्रम में line up करते हैं।

gas को heat कीजिए और पूरी curve respond करती है। peak दाईं ओर slide होता है जैसे molecules तेज़ होते हैं, और curve flatten होकर एक wider range पर फैलती है, पर total area, यानी molecules की total संख्या, fixed रहती है।

same temperature पर एक heavier gas लीजिए और curve बाईं ओर squeeze होती है। heavier molecules वही average kinetic energy रखते हैं, तो उन्हें धीमे चलना पड़ता है। equal energy, unequal speeds, exam questions का एक बड़ा हिस्सा समझा देता है।

एक reading rule ज़रूरी है। curve को एक area की तरह पढ़िए, height की तरह नहीं। किसी भी speed interval में molecules का fraction वहाँ curve के नीचे का area है, और किसी एक speed पर height खुद एक probability नहीं है। total area हमेशा one है।

segments.text: <curious>Now the derivation.</curious> We carry over two results and simply set them equal, and the kinetic meaning of temperature falls out.
From the pressure derivation, pressure times volume is one third N m mean square speed. From the ideal gas law in molecular form, pressure times volume is N k B T. Both describe the same gas.
So set the two expressions equal, as the picture shows, and cancel the number of molecules, since the result is per molecule.

That leaves one third m mean square speed equals k B T, which rearranges to one half m mean square speed equals three halves k B T. The left side is the average translational kinetic energy of one molecule, so temperature is a direct measure of it, the same for all gases.

Solve for the r m s speed and you get the root of three k B T over m. Scaling top and bottom inside the root by Avogadro's number converts it to the root of three R T over M, and the density form follows at once.

The most probable speed is the peak of the distribution, found by setting the derivative of the Maxwell curve to zero. The exponential never vanishes and zero speed is a minimum, so the maximum needs the remaining bracket to vanish.

That gives the most probable speed as the root of two k B T over m. It carries the smallest coefficient, root two, because it marks the peak, while the averaging behind the mean and the energy-weighting behind the r m s both pull their values up into the fast tail.
अब derivation। हम दो results आगे ले जाते हैं और उन्हें बस बराबर रख देते हैं, और temperature का kinetic meaning निकल आता है।
pressure derivation से, pressure into volume one third N m mean square speed है। molecular form में ideal gas law से, pressure into volume N k B T है। दोनों एक ही gas बताते हैं।
तो दोनों expressions बराबर रखिए, जैसा picture दिखाता है, और molecules की संख्या cancel कीजिए, क्योंकि result per molecule है।

इससे बचता है one third m mean square speed बराबर k B T, जो rearrange होकर one half m mean square speed बराबर three halves k B T बनता है। बायाँ हिस्सा एक molecule की average translational kinetic energy है, तो temperature उसका सीधा माप है, सभी gases के लिए एक जैसा।
r m s speed के लिए solve कीजिए तो three k B T over m का root मिलता है। root के अंदर ऊपर-नीचे Avogadro number से scale करने पर यह three R T over M का root बन जाता है, और density form तुरंत आ जाता है।

most probable speed distribution का peak है, जो Maxwell curve के derivative को zero रखकर मिलता है। exponential कभी vanish नहीं होता और zero speed एक minimum है, तो maximum के लिए बचा हुआ bracket vanish होना चाहिए।

इससे most probable speed two k B T over m का root मिलता है। यह सबसे छोटा coefficient, root two, रखता है, क्योंकि यह peak को mark करता है, जबकि mean के पीछे की averaging और r m s के पीछे की energy-weighting दोनों अपने values को fast tail में ऊपर खींचती हैं।

sections.title: Speeds, temperature, and the distribution

board_events.text: The speed formulas, gathered
Units: M in kg/mol, T in kelvin, kB = 1.38 x 10^-23 J/K. Monatomic internal energy U = (3/2) nRT.

segments.text: <curious>Here is the toolkit</curious> for this subtopic, the kinetic interpretation of temperature, the three speeds, their fixed ordering, and the distribution itself.

The central bridge: one half m mean square speed equals three halves k B T, so the average translational energy per molecule depends only on temperature. For N molecules or n moles the total is three halves N k B T, equivalently three halves n R T.
The three molecular speeds: root three R T over M for r m s, root eight R T over pi M for the average, and root two R T over M for the most probable.

Their order and ratio, true at any temperature for any gas: r m s is largest, then average, then most probable, in the ratio root three to root eight over pi to root two, about one point two two to one point one three to one. Remember the hook R A M, largest to smallest.

All three share the same scaling: every speed grows as the square root of temperature and falls as one over the square root of molar mass. So a speed ratio is just the root of the temperature ratio at fixed mass, or the root of the inverse mass ratio at fixed temperature.
And the Maxwell-Boltzmann speed distribution itself: the fraction of molecules between v and v plus d v. Its peak sits at the most probable speed, and the total area under it is one.

Two unit warnings. Molar mass must be in kilograms per mole, and temperature in kelvin. And for a monatomic ideal gas this translational energy is the entire internal energy, three halves n R T, a result used constantly in thermodynamics.
यह रहा इस subtopic का toolkit, temperature का kinetic interpretation, तीन speeds, उनका fixed ordering, और distribution खुद।

central bridge: one half m mean square speed बराबर three halves k B T, तो per molecule average translational energy सिर्फ़ temperature पर depend करती है। N molecules या n moles के लिए total three halves N k B T है, यानी three halves n R T।
तीन molecular speeds: r m s के लिए root three R T over M, average के लिए root eight R T over pi M, और most probable के लिए root two R T over M।

उनका order और ratio, किसी भी temperature पर किसी भी gas के लिए सच: r m s सबसे बड़ा, फिर average, फिर most probable, ratio root three to root eight over pi to root two में, करीब one point two two to one point one three to one। hook R A M याद रखिए, largest से smallest।

तीनों एक ही scaling share करते हैं: हर speed temperature के square root के साथ बढ़ती है और molar mass के square root के inverse के साथ घटती है। तो एक speed ratio बस fixed mass पर temperature ratio का root है, या fixed temperature पर inverse mass ratio का root।
और Maxwell-Boltzmann speed distribution खुद: v और v plus d v के बीच molecules का fraction। इसका peak most probable speed पर है, और इसके नीचे total area one है।

दो unit warnings। molar mass kilograms per mole में होना चाहिए, और temperature kelvin में। <whisper>और एक monatomic ideal gas के लिए यह translational energy पूरी internal energy है</whisper>, three halves n R T, thermodynamics में लगातार इस्तेमाल होने वाला result।

sections.title: Worked example: rms speed of nitrogen

board_events.text: CBSE example: nitrogen at 27 degrees Celsius
Fix the units first: M = 28 x 10^-3 kg/mol, T = 300 K.
Convert M to kg/mol: leaving it in g/mol inflates the answer by sqrt(1000) ~ 32 times.
The other two follow from the fixed ratio: vav ~476, vmp ~422 m/s; order is rms, then average, then most probable.

segments.text: <curious>Calculate the r m s speed</curious> of nitrogen molecules, molar mass twenty eight grams per mole, at twenty seven degrees Celsius. Take R as eight point three one four.
First fix the units. Molar mass becomes twenty eight times ten to the minus three kilograms per mole, and the temperature becomes three hundred kelvin.
Use r m s equals the root of three R T over M.
Substitute: three times eight point three one four times three hundred, over twenty eight times ten to the minus three, is about two point six seven two times ten to the five.
The square root is about five hundred seventeen metres per second.

Mind the conversion of molar mass to kilograms per mole. Leaving it in grams per mole would inflate the answer by the root of a thousand, about thirty two times, the single most common error in this topic.

The other two speeds follow at once from the fixed ratio, without redoing the calculation: the average is about four hundred seventy six and the most probable about four hundred twenty two metres per second, confirming the order r m s largest, then average, then most probable.
nitrogen molecules की r m s speed निकालिए, molar mass twenty eight grams per mole, twenty seven degrees Celsius पर। R को eight point three one four लीजिए।
पहले units ठीक कीजिए। molar mass twenty eight times ten to the minus three kilograms per mole बनता है, और temperature three hundred kelvin।
r m s बराबर three R T over M का root इस्तेमाल कीजिए।
substitute कीजिए: three into eight point three one four into three hundred, बटा twenty eight times ten to the minus three, करीब two point six seven two times ten to the five है।
इसका square root करीब five hundred seventeen metres per second है।

molar mass को kilograms per mole में convert करने का ध्यान रखिए। <whisper>इसे grams per mole में छोड़ना answer को root of a thousand से बढ़ा देता है</whisper>, करीब thirty two गुना, इस topic की सबसे common error।

बाकी दो speeds fixed ratio से तुरंत आ जाते हैं, calculation दोहराए बिना: average करीब four hundred seventy six और most probable करीब four hundred twenty two metres per second, order r m s सबसे बड़ा, फिर average, फिर most probable confirm करते हुए।

sections.title: Worked example: hydrogen versus oxygen

board_events.text: NEET speed trap: which gas is faster?
At fixed T, speed goes as 1 over root M, so the ratio is the root of the inverse mass ratio.
Hydrogen molecules move 4 times as fast as oxygen at the same temperature.
Trap: do not take the mass ratio 32/2 = 16 directly; take its root. And the lighter gas is always faster.
One relation handles every 'which gas is faster' question: vA/vB = sqrt(MB/MA).

segments.text: <curious>At the same temperature</curious>, find the ratio of the r m s speed of hydrogen, molar mass two, to that of oxygen, molar mass thirty two.
At fixed temperature the r m s speed goes as one over the square root of the molar mass, so the ratio is the square root of the inverse mass ratio.
So the ratio of hydrogen's speed to oxygen's is the root of thirty two over two.
That is the root of sixteen, which is four.
So hydrogen molecules move four times as fast as oxygen molecules at the same temperature.

Two slips lurk. Do not take the mass ratio thirty two over two directly as sixteen; take its square root. And do not invert it and call oxygen faster, because the lighter gas is always faster at a given temperature.

A two-second sanity check, light equals fast, kills the wrong option instantly. And a single relation, speed of A over speed of B equals the root of molar mass B over molar mass A, handles every which-gas-is-faster question on the paper.
same temperature पर, hydrogen की r m s speed, molar mass two, और oxygen की, molar mass thirty two, का ratio निकालिए।
fixed temperature पर r m s speed molar mass के square root के inverse के जैसे चलती है, तो ratio inverse mass ratio का square root है।
तो hydrogen की speed और oxygen की speed का ratio thirty two over two का root है।
यह sixteen का root है, यानी four।
तो hydrogen molecules same temperature पर oxygen molecules से four गुना तेज़ move करते हैं।

दो slips छिपे हैं। mass ratio thirty two over two को सीधे sixteen मत लीजिए; उसका square root लीजिए। और इसे invert करके oxygen को तेज़ मत कहिए, क्योंकि लाइटर gas दिए गए temperature पर हमेशा तेज़ होती है।

एक two-second sanity check, light बराबर fast, गलत option तुरंत खत्म कर देता है। और एक single relation, speed of A over speed of B बराबर molar mass B over molar mass A का root, <whisper>paper के हर which-gas-is-faster question को handle करता है।</whisper>

sections.title: Worked example: matching rms speeds across gases

board_events.text: JEE Main example: cool helium to match nitrogen
Setting the two rms speeds equal, the shared factors cancel: equal speeds reduce to equal T over M.
Helium must be cooled to 50 K: being much lighter, it must be far colder to match slower nitrogen.
Key step: 'equal rms speeds' reduces to 'equal T/M'. Recognise it and the rest is arithmetic.

segments.text: <curious>At what temperature</curious> will the r m s speed of helium atoms, molar mass four, equal the r m s speed of nitrogen molecules, molar mass twenty eight, held at three hundred fifty kelvin?
Setting the two r m s speeds equal, the shared factors cancel and equal speeds reduce simply to equal temperature over molar mass.
So temperature over molar mass for helium equals temperature over molar mass for nitrogen.
Solve for helium's temperature: three hundred fifty times four over twenty eight.
That is fifty kelvin.

Helium must be cooled all the way to fifty kelvin. This makes physical sense: helium is much lighter, so to match the slower nitrogen it must have far less kinetic energy, hence a far lower temperature.
The key step is recognising that equal r m s speeds reduces to equal temperature over molar mass. Spot that, and everything else is one line of arithmetic.
किस temperature पर helium atoms की r m s speed, molar mass four, nitrogen molecules की r m s speed के बराबर होगी, molar mass twenty eight, जो three hundred fifty kelvin पर हैं?
दोनों r m s speeds को बराबर रखने पर, shared factors cancel हो जाते हैं और equal speeds बस equal temperature over molar mass तक सिमट जाते हैं।
तो helium के लिए temperature over molar mass nitrogen के लिए temperature over molar mass के बराबर है।
helium का temperature solve कीजिए: three hundred fifty into four over twenty eight।
यह fifty kelvin है।
helium को fifty kelvin तक cool करना पड़ेगा। यह physical sense बनाता है: helium कहीं हल्का है, तो slower nitrogen से match करने के लिए उसे कहीं कम kinetic energy चाहिए, इसलिए कहीं lower temperature।
key step यह पहचानना है कि equal r m s speeds बराबर equal temperature over molar mass तक सिमट जाता है। इसे पहचानिए, और <whisper>बाकी सब एक line arithmetic है।</whisper>

board_events.text: Indeed vrms (6.63) exceeds vav (6.00). Now the deeper reason.
Squaring weights large speeds: the 10 adds 100 to the squared-sum but only 10 to the plain sum. The fast tail drags vrms up.
This is the mean-square-exceeds-square-of-mean inequality, strict whenever speeds spread; so vrms exceeds vav exceeds vmp, always.

segments.text: <curious>Five molecules have speeds</curious>, in arbitrary units, of two, four, six, eight, and ten. Compute the average and r m s speeds and verify r m s exceeds the average. Then explain why, for a real gas, r m s always exceeds the average.
The picture already hints at the answer. The molecule at ten looms far larger once you square the speeds.
The average speed is the plain mean, thirty over five, which is six point zero zero units.
For the r m s, average the squares: four plus sixteen plus thirty six plus sixty four plus one hundred, over five, is forty four. Its square root is about six point six three units.
Indeed the r m s, six point six three, exceeds the average, six point zero zero. Now for the deeper reason.

The r m s averages the squares of the speeds, and squaring weights large speeds disproportionately. A molecule at ten contributes one hundred to the squared sum but only ten to the plain sum, so the high-speed tail of the Maxwell distribution drags the r m s above the average.

Mathematically this is the statement that the mean of the squares is at least the square of the mean, with equality only if every molecule had the same speed. A real gas always has a spread, so the inequality is strict, and r m s stays above average, above most probable.

सचमुच r m s, six point six three, average, six point zero zero, से बड़ा है। <excited>अब गहरा कारण।</excited>

sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips: speeds and the Maxwell curve

board_events.text: The high-yield traps of this subtopic
Molar mass in vrms = sqrt(3RT/M) must be kg/mol; using g/mol inflates every speed by ~32.
Celsius instead of kelvin: always convert before taking the square root.
Coefficients: sqrt(3) rms, sqrt(8/pi) average, sqrt(2) most probable, in RAM order. Only the average carries pi.
Average velocity (vector) is zero; average speed (scalar) is not. 'Average velocity' questions test this.
The height P(v) is not a probability: only the area under a stretch of curve gives a fraction. Total area stays 1.
Pro-tip: for compare-two-gases or change-T problems, use v proportional to sqrt(T/M); one line, no calculator.

segments.text: <curious>This subtopic is extremely high-yield</curious>, so the traps repay careful naming. Five slips and one pro-tip.

First, the molar mass in the speed formula must be in kilograms per mole. Using grams per mole inflates every speed by the root of a thousand, about thirty two times, the most common error in board and entrance scripts.
Second, like every gas relation these use absolute temperature. Always convert Celsius to kelvin before taking the square root.

Third, do not confuse the three speeds or their coefficients. Root three for r m s, root eight over pi for the average, root two for the most probable, in R A M order. Only the average carries a pi, a handy fingerprint.

Fourth, keep average velocity and average speed apart. The mean velocity vector is zero by isotropy, but the mean speed is not. Questions that say average velocity are usually testing whether you will wrongly plug in the average speed.

Fifth, do not misread the Maxwell curve. The height is not a probability; only the area under a stretch of the curve gives the fraction of molecules in that range. And the total area is always one, so heating redistributes molecules into the faster tail but never adds or removes any.

And the pro-tip: for compare-two-gases or change-the-temperature problems, never compute full speeds. Use speed proportional to the root of temperature over molar mass directly. One line, no calculator, no unit errors.
यह subtopic बेहद high-yield है, तो traps को ध्यान से नाम देना फ़ायदेमंद है। पाँच slips और एक pro-tip।

पहला, speed formula में molar mass kilograms per mole में होना चाहिए। grams per mole इस्तेमाल करना हर speed को root of a thousand से, करीब thirty two गुना, बढ़ा देता है, board और entrance scripts की सबसे common error।
दूसरा, हर gas relation की तरह ये absolute temperature इस्तेमाल करते हैं। square root लेने से पहले हमेशा Celsius को kelvin में convert कीजिए।

तीसरा, तीन speeds या उनके coefficients को confuse मत कीजिए। r m s के लिए root three, average के लिए root eight over pi, most probable के लिए root two, R A M order में। सिर्फ़ average में pi होता है, एक handy fingerprint।

चौथा, average velocity और average speed को अलग रखिए। mean velocity vector isotropy से zero है, पर mean speed नहीं। जो questions average velocity कहते हैं वे अक्सर test करते हैं कि क्या आप गलती से average speed plug कर देंगे।

पाँचवाँ, Maxwell curve को गलत मत पढ़िए। height एक probability नहीं है; सिर्फ़ curve के एक हिस्से के नीचे का area उस range में molecules का fraction देता है। और total area हमेशा one है, तो heating molecules को faster tail में redistribute करती है पर कभी add या remove नहीं करती।

और pro-tip: compare-two-gases या change-the-temperature problems के लिए, कभी full speeds मत निकालिए। speed को temperature over molar mass के root के proportional सीधे इस्तेमाल कीजिए। <whisper>एक line, कोई calculator नहीं, कोई unit error नहीं।</whisper>

board_events.text: Diatomic (nitrogen): 3 translation + 2 rotation = 5 at room T; +2 vibration = 7 when hot.
Spinning about the bond axis stores nothing: the moment of inertia along the bond is ~0, so diatomic counts 2 rotations, monatomic 0.
Non-linear polyatomic (water): 3 translation + 3 rotation = 6 at room T. Vibration is frozen out at ordinary temperatures.
Room-T defaults: f = 3 (mono), 5 (diatomic), 6 (non-linear poly). Vibration adds 2 each when hot; hydrogen rotation itself freezes below ~50 K.

segments.text: <curious>So far our molecules have only flown</curious>, moving through space. But a real molecule can do more: a dumbbell-shaped oxygen molecule can also tumble, and when hot its two atoms can vibrate along their bond like masses on a spring. Each independent way of moving is a place to store energy, and we call it a degree of freedom.

Think of how a coin can carry state. It can slide across a table, that is translation; it can spin on the spot, that is rotation; and if it were soft it could wobble and flex, that is vibration. A gas molecule shares these same categories, and counting them is the whole game of this subtopic.
The picture lays out the count. A point-like atom like helium is a marble: it can only slide, in three independent directions, so it has three translational degrees of freedom and nothing more.

A diatomic molecule like nitrogen is a tiny dumbbell. It slides in three directions and tumbles end over end about two axes, giving five degrees of freedom at room temperature. Heat it enough and the bond begins to vibrate, adding two more, for seven in all.

But why only two rotations, not three? Spinning about the bond axis itself stores nothing. Rotational kinetic energy is one half I omega squared, and the moment of inertia about the line joining the two atoms is vanishingly small, since almost all the mass sits on that line. With that moment of inertia near zero, no meaningful energy hides there. The same argument gives a monatomic atom zero rotational modes.

A non-linear polyatomic molecule like water tumbles about all three axes, so it carries three translational plus three rotational, six in all at room temperature. And a crucial caution: vibrational modes are frozen out at ordinary temperatures and only switch on when it is hot, so unless a problem says otherwise, use the room-temperature counts.

So keep the defaults: three for monatomic, five for diatomic, six for non-linear polyatomic, with vibration adding two more only when hot. This freezing-out is quantum mechanics quietly intruding on a classical theory, and for hydrogen even the rotation freezes out below about fifty kelvin.

अब तक हमारे molecules सिर्फ़ उड़े हैं, space में move करते हुए। पर एक real molecule इससे ज़्यादा कर सकता है: एक dumbbell-shaped oxygen molecule tumble भी कर सकता है, और गर्म होने पर उसके दो atoms bond के साथ vibrate कर सकते हैं, spring पर masses की तरह। move करने का हर independent तरीका energy स्टोर करने की एक जगह है, और उसे हम degree of freedom कहते हैं।

सोचिए एक coin कैसे state रख सकता है। वह table पर slide कर सकता है, यह translation है; एक जगह spin कर सकता है, यह rotation है; और अगर soft हो तो wobble और flex कर सकता है, यह vibration है। एक gas molecule यही categories share करता है, और उन्हें गिनना ही इस subtopic का पूरा खेल है।
picture यह count दिखाता है। helium जैसा point-like atom एक marble है: यह सिर्फ़ slide कर सकता है, तीन independent directions में, तो उसके पास तीन translational degrees of freedom हैं और कुछ नहीं।

nitrogen जैसा diatomic molecule एक tiny dumbbell है। यह तीन directions में slide करता है और दो axes के बारे में end over end tumble करता है, room temperature पर पाँच degrees of freedom देते हुए। इसे काफ़ी गर्म कीजिए और bond vibrate करने लगता है, दो और जोड़ते हुए, कुल सात।

पर सिर्फ़ दो rotations क्यों, तीन नहीं? bond axis के बारे में spin करना खुद कुछ स्टोर नहीं करता। rotational kinetic energy one half I omega squared है, और दोनों atoms को जोड़ने वाली line के बारे में moment of inertia बेहद छोटा है, क्योंकि लगभग सारा mass उसी line पर बैठता है। उस moment of inertia के near zero होने से, वहाँ कोई meaningful energy नहीं छिपती। यही argument एक monatomic atom को zero rotational modes देता है।

water जैसा non-linear polyatomic molecule तीनों axes के बारे में tumble करता है, तो यह तीन translational plus तीन rotational रखता है, room temperature पर कुल छह। और एक ज़रूरी caution: vibrational modes ordinary temperatures पर frozen out होते हैं और सिर्फ़ गर्म होने पर switch on होते हैं, तो जब तक problem कुछ और न कहे, room-temperature counts इस्तेमाल कीजिए।

तो defaults याद रखिए: monatomic के लिए तीन, diatomic के लिए पाँच, non-linear polyatomic के लिए छह, vibration सिर्फ़ गर्म होने पर दो और जोड़ते हुए। <whisper>यह freezing-out एक classical theory पर quantum mechanics का चुपचाप दख़ल है</whisper>, और hydrogen के लिए तो rotation भी करीब fifty kelvin के नीचे freeze हो जाता है।

board_events.text: U depends only on T. For monatomic (f = 3), U = (3/2) nRT, the translational energy from Sub-topic 3.
From U = (f/2)nRT flow the specific heats Cv, Cp and their ratio gamma: the key that unlocks the rest of the subtopic.

segments.text: <curious>Now the elegant part.</curious> Nature is scrupulously fair about how it shares thermal energy: it dumps exactly the same amount into every single degree of freedom, no matter what kind. This is the law of equipartition of energy.

And the amount is fixed: one half k B T per molecule for each degree of freedom, or equivalently one half R T per mole. Energy is partitioned equally among all available modes, translation, rotation and vibration alike.
The bars say it at a glance: each mode receives an equal share, and stacking them up gives the molecule its total average energy.
So a molecule with f degrees of freedom carries an average energy of f times one half k B T, that is f over two k B T.
Multiply by the number of molecules and use that Avogadro's number times k B equals R. The internal energy of n moles is f over two n R T. This one line is the master key of the subtopic.

Notice what this says. The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on its temperature, never on its volume or pressure. And for a monatomic gas, with f equal to three, it becomes three halves n R T, exactly the translational energy we met in the previous subtopic.

From this single expression for the internal energy flow the two specific heats and their ratio gamma, which we derive next. Equipartition, in short, turns a count of modes straight into thermodynamics.
अब elegant हिस्सा। nature thermal energy बाँटने में बेहद fair है: यह हर एक degree of freedom में ठीक उतनी ही मात्रा डालती है, चाहे वह किसी भी तरह का हो। यह law of equipartition of energy है।

और मात्रा fixed है: हर degree of freedom के लिए per molecule one half k B T, या equivalently per mole one half R T। energy सारे available modes में equally बँटती है, translation, rotation और vibration सब में एक जैसी।
bars एक नज़र में यह कह देते हैं: हर mode को equal share मिलता है, और उन्हें ढेर करने पर molecule को उसकी total average energy मिलती है।
तो f degrees of freedom वाला एक molecule f into one half k B T की average energy रखता है, यानी f over two k B T।
molecules की संख्या से multiply कीजिए और इस्तेमाल कीजिए कि Avogadro number into k B बराबर R। n moles की internal energy f over two n R T है। यही एक line इस subtopic की master key है।

ध्यान दीजिए यह क्या कहता है। एक ideal gas की internal energy सिर्फ़ उसके temperature पर depend करती है, कभी volume या pressure पर नहीं। और एक monatomic gas के लिए, f बराबर तीन के साथ, यह three halves n R T बन जाती है, ठीक वही translational energy जो हमने पिछले subtopic में देखी।

internal energy के इसी एक expression से दोनों specific heats और उनका ratio gamma निकलते हैं, जो हम आगे derive करते हैं। <whisper>संक्षेप में, equipartition modes की गिनती को सीधे thermodynamics में बदल देती है।</whisper>

board_events.text: Because gamma depends only on f, measuring gamma reveals the atomicity of a gas. More modes soak up heat, lowering gamma toward 1.
Handy inverses: Cv = R/(gamma - 1), Cp = gamma R/(gamma - 1). More atoms means smaller gamma.

segments.text: <curious>With the internal energy in hand</curious>, the specific heats follow in four clean steps. This is the derivation that lets a single measured number reveal what a gas is made of.
Step one, the internal energy from equipartition: f over two n R T.

Step two, the molar heat capacity at constant volume. At constant volume no work is done, so all the heat goes into internal energy; differentiating U per mole with respect to temperature gives C v equals f over two R.

Step three, the constant-pressure capacity. Heated at constant pressure the gas also does expansion work, and Mayer's relation captures this as C p minus C v equals R. So C p is C v plus R, that is f over two plus one, times R.
Step four, divide the two. Gamma equals C p over C v, which simplifies to one plus two over f. So the entire ratio is decided by the number of degrees of freedom alone.

The table collects the standard results. Monatomic gives gamma five thirds, about one point six seven; diatomic gives seven fifths, one point four zero; non-linear polyatomic gives four thirds, about one point three three.

Here is why this matters so much. Because gamma depends only on f, measuring gamma experimentally tells you the atomicity of a gas at a glance. And the trend is intuitive: the more ways a molecule can store energy, the more heat it soaks up without its temperature rising as fast, which lowers gamma toward one.

Two inverses are worth keeping: C v equals R over gamma minus one, and C p equals gamma R over gamma minus one. They turn a known gamma straight back into the heat capacities whenever a problem hands you the ratio.
internal energy हाथ में होने पर, specific heats चार clean steps में निकल आते हैं। यह वह derivation है जो एक single measured number को यह बताने देती है कि एक gas किससे बना है।
step one, equipartition से internal energy: f over two n R T।

step two, constant volume पर molar heat capacity। constant volume पर कोई work नहीं होता, तो सारी heat internal energy में जाती है; U को per mole temperature के respect में differentiate करने पर C v बराबर f over two R मिलता है।

step three, constant-pressure capacity। constant pressure पर गर्म करने पर gas expansion work भी करती है, और Mayer's relation इसे C p minus C v बराबर R के रूप में पकड़ता है। तो C p, C v plus R है, यानी f over two plus one, into R।
step four, दोनों को divide कीजिए। gamma बराबर C p over C v, जो simplify होकर one plus two over f बनता है। तो पूरा ratio सिर्फ़ degrees of freedom की संख्या से तय होता है।

table standard results इकट्ठा करता है। monatomic gamma five thirds देता है, करीब one point six seven; diatomic seven fifths देता है, one point four zero; non-linear polyatomic four thirds देता है, करीब one point three three।

यही कारण है कि यह इतना matter करता है। चूँकि gamma सिर्फ़ f पर depend करता है, gamma को experimentally मापना आपको एक नज़र में gas की atomicity बता देता है। और trend intuitive है: एक molecule energy स्टोर करने के जितने ज़्यादा तरीके रखता है, उतनी ज़्यादा heat वह temperature उतनी तेज़ी से बढ़ाए बिना सोख लेता है, जो gamma को one की ओर घटाता है।

दो inverses रखने लायक़ हैं: C v बराबर R over gamma minus one, और C p बराबर gamma R over gamma minus one। <whisper>जब भी problem आपको ratio देता है ये एक known gamma को सीधे heat capacities में वापस बदल देते हैं।</whisper>

segments.text: <curious>The second big idea of this subtopic</curious> is about what a molecule does between collisions. A molecule in air does not sail smoothly across the room; it ricochets off its neighbours billions of times a second, tracing a frantic zig-zag.

The mean free path, written lambda, is the average straight-line distance a molecule covers between two successive collisions. It is tiny but not vanishingly so: in ordinary air it is about a hundred times the molecular size, which is exactly why gases are mostly free with only occasional collisions.
The picture shows the idea: a tracked molecule bounces among its neighbours, and lambda is the average length of one of those straight segments.

To derive it, model molecules as hard spheres of diameter d. A moving molecule collides whenever two centres come within d, so it sweeps out a cylinder of cross-section pi d squared. In time t it sweeps a volume pi d squared v t, containing n pi d squared v t centres, and dividing the distance travelled by that count gives lambda equals one over n pi d squared.

One refinement: the simple count assumed only one molecule moves. Since all of them move, what matters is the relative speed, and averaging it introduces a factor of root two in the denominator. Substituting the number density from the ideal gas law gives the pressure-temperature form, lambda equals k B T over root two pi d squared P.

The dependences are now explicit. At fixed pressure lambda grows with temperature; at fixed temperature it falls as pressure rises; and it falls with the square of the molecular diameter. The quantity pi d squared is the collision cross-section, the effective target a molecule presents.

Once lambda is known, the collision frequency follows at once. A molecule covers one mean free path between collisions while moving at the average speed, so the number of collisions per second is v average over lambda, and its reciprocal is the mean time between collisions.

This single formula ties the whole chapter together: the average speed comes from the Maxwell distribution, lambda from the collision geometry here, and the number density from the ideal gas law. In ordinary air a molecule collides several billion times every second, a vivid measure of how busy a still volume of air really is.

इस subtopic का दूसरा बड़ा idea यह है कि एक molecule collisions के बीच क्या करता है। हवा में एक molecule कमरे के पार smoothly नहीं तैरता; यह अपने neighbours से billions of times per second ricochet करता है, एक frantic zig-zag बनाते हुए।

mean free path, जिसे lambda लिखते हैं, वह average straight-line distance है जो एक molecule दो successive collisions के बीच तय करता है। यह छोटा है पर बेहद छोटा नहीं: ordinary हवा में यह molecular size का करीब सौ गुना है, इसीलिए gases ज़्यादातर free होते हैं सिर्फ़ occasional collisions के साथ।
picture idea दिखाता है: एक tracked molecule अपने neighbours के बीच bounce करता है, और lambda उन straight segments में से एक की average length है।

इसे derive करने के लिए, molecules को diameter d के hard spheres मानिए। एक moving molecule तब collide करता है जब दो centres d के भीतर आ जाएँ, तो यह cross-section pi d squared का एक cylinder sweep करता है। time t में यह pi d squared v t volume sweep करता है, जिसमें n pi d squared v t centres हैं, और तय की गई distance को उस count से divide करने पर lambda बराबर one over n pi d squared मिलता है।

एक refinement: simple count ने माना कि सिर्फ़ एक molecule move करता है। चूँकि सब move करते हैं, जो matter करता है वह relative speed है, और उसका average लेने पर denominator में root two का factor आ जाता है। ideal gas law से number density substitute करने पर pressure-temperature form मिलता है, lambda बराबर k B T over root two pi d squared P।

dependences अब explicit हैं। fixed pressure पर lambda temperature के साथ बढ़ता है; fixed temperature पर pressure बढ़ने पर घटता है; और molecular diameter के square के साथ घटता है। quantity pi d squared collision cross-section है, वह effective target जो एक molecule पेश करता है।

lambda पता होने पर collision frequency तुरंत आ जाती है। एक molecule average speed पर चलते हुए collisions के बीच एक mean free path तय करता है, तो प्रति second collisions की संख्या v average over lambda है, और उसका reciprocal collisions के बीच का mean time है।

यह एक formula पूरे chapter को जोड़ देता है: average speed Maxwell distribution से आती है, lambda यहाँ की collision geometry से, और number density ideal gas law से। <whisper>ordinary हवा में एक molecule हर second कई अरब बार collide करता है</whisper>, इस बात का एक जीवंत माप कि एक still हवा कितनी busy होती है।

sections.subtopic: Degrees of Freedom and Mean Free Path
sections.title: The toolkit: freedom, energy, heat, and free path

board_events.text: This subtopic's formulas, gathered
Molar quantities (Cv, Cp, U) use R; per-molecule energies use kB. Temperature always in kelvin.

segments.text: <curious>Let us gather this subtopic's formulas</curious>, the equipartition results, the specific heats, and the mean free path with its collision frequency.
Equipartition gives one half k B T per degree of freedom per molecule, so a molecule averages f over two k B T, and n moles have internal energy f over two n R T, a function of temperature alone.
The specific heats: C v is f over two R, C p is that plus R, and gamma is one plus two over f. The inverse, C v equals R over gamma minus one, is the fastest route when gamma is given.

The three benchmarks to memorise: monatomic, f three, gamma five thirds; diatomic, f five, gamma seven fifths; non-linear polyatomic, f six, gamma four thirds. About one point six seven, one point four zero, and one point three three.

The mean free path is one over root two pi d squared n, equivalently k B T over root two pi d squared P. So lambda grows with temperature, falls inversely with pressure, and falls with the square of the diameter.
The collision frequency is the average speed over lambda, which also equals root two pi d squared n times the average speed. Its reciprocal is the mean time between collisions.

Equipartition reaches beyond gases. In a solid each atom vibrates about its lattice site along three axes, six degrees of freedom, giving a molar heat capacity of three R, about twenty five, the law of Dulong and Petit. Treating each of water's three atoms the same way gives nine R, about seventy five, matching the measured value.

One discipline to hold onto. Molar quantities, the heat capacities and the internal energy, use R; per-molecule energies use k B. Mixing them up costs a factor of Avogadro's number. And as always, temperature goes in kelvin.
चलिए इस subtopic की formulas इकट्ठा करते हैं, equipartition results, specific heats, और mean free path अपनी collision frequency के साथ।

equipartition per molecule per degree of freedom one half k B T देता है, तो एक molecule f over two k B T average करता है, और n moles की internal energy f over two n R T है, सिर्फ़ temperature का function।
specific heats: C v, f over two R है, C p उसमें R जोड़कर, और gamma one plus two over f है। inverse, C v बराबर R over gamma minus one, तब सबसे तेज़ रास्ता है जब gamma दिया हो।

याद करने के तीन benchmarks: monatomic, f तीन, gamma five thirds; diatomic, f पाँच, gamma seven fifths; non-linear polyatomic, f छह, gamma four thirds। करीब one point six seven, one point four zero, और one point three three।

mean free path one over root two pi d squared n है, equivalently k B T over root two pi d squared P। तो lambda temperature के साथ बढ़ता है, pressure के inverse के साथ घटता है, और diameter के square के साथ घटता है।
collision frequency, average speed over lambda है, जो root two pi d squared n into average speed के भी बराबर है। उसका reciprocal collisions के बीच का mean time है।

equipartition gases से आगे पहुँचती है। एक solid में हर atom अपनी lattice site के बारे में तीन axes के साथ vibrate करता है, छह degrees of freedom, तीन R की molar heat capacity देते हुए, करीब पच्चीस, Dulong और Petit का law। water के तीन atoms में से हर एक को इसी तरह treat करने पर nine R मिलता है, करीब पचहत्तर, measured value से match करते हुए।

एक discipline पकड़े रखिए। molar quantities, heat capacities और internal energy, R इस्तेमाल करते हैं; per-molecule energies k B इस्तेमाल करते हैं। इन्हें मिलाना Avogadro number का factor खर्च कराता है। <whisper>और हमेशा की तरह, temperature kelvin में जाता है।</whisper>

sections.title: Worked example: internal energy of a diatomic gas

board_events.text: CBSE example: three moles of a diatomic gas
Only translation and rotation active means room temperature, so f = 5 (not 7).
Key: f = 5 here, not 7. 'Only translation and rotation' means room-temperature behaviour; vibration is excluded.
Internal energy needs only f, n, and T; it never depends on volume or pressure.

segments.text: <curious>Calculate the internal energy</curious> of three moles of a diatomic ideal gas at three hundred kelvin, assuming only translational and rotational modes are active. Take R as eight point three one four.
Because only translation and rotation are active, this is the room-temperature case, so f is five, not seven. We use the equipartition internal energy directly.
Write the internal energy as f over two n R T.
Substitute f equal five, n equal three, R equal eight point three one four, and temperature three hundred: five halves times three times eight point three one four times three hundred.
That works out to about one point eight seven times ten to the four joules.
The key decision was using f equal five, not seven. The phrase only translational and rotational modes signals room-temperature behaviour, so the vibrational contribution is excluded.

And the wider takeaway: internal energy needs only the degrees of freedom, the mole count, and the temperature. It never depends on the volume or the pressure, because for an ideal gas U is a function of temperature alone.
एक diatomic ideal gas के तीन moles की internal energy निकालिए three hundred kelvin पर, मानते हुए कि सिर्फ़ translational और rotational modes active हैं। R को eight point three one four लीजिए।
चूँकि सिर्फ़ translation और rotation active हैं, यह room-temperature case है, तो f पाँच है, सात नहीं। हम सीधे equipartition internal energy इस्तेमाल करते हैं।
internal energy को f over two n R T लिखिए।
f बराबर पाँच, n बराबर तीन, R बराबर eight point three one four, और temperature three hundred substitute कीजिए: five halves into three into eight point three one four into three hundred।
यह करीब one point eight seven times ten to the four joules निकलता है।
key decision f बराबर पाँच इस्तेमाल करना था, सात नहीं। only translational and rotational modes वाक्यांश room-temperature behaviour का संकेत देता है, तो vibrational contribution excluded है।

और व्यापक takeaway: internal energy को सिर्फ़ degrees of freedom, mole count, और temperature चाहिए। <whisper>यह कभी volume या pressure पर depend नहीं करती</whisper>, क्योंकि एक ideal gas के लिए U सिर्फ़ temperature का function है।

sections.title: Worked example: reading atomicity from gamma

board_events.text: NEET speed trap: gamma gives the atomicity
Rearrange gamma = 1 + 2/f for f: this gives f = 2/(gamma - 1).
f = 5 means diatomic; Cv = (5/2)R ~ 20.8 J mol^-1 K^-1.
Trap: f = 2/(gamma - 1), NOT 2/gamma. The '-1' in the denominator is the whole game.
Memorise the trio: gamma = 1.67 mono, 1.40 di, 1.33 poly, to identify a gas by sight.

segments.text: <curious>The ratio of specific heats</curious> of a gas is found to be one point four zero. Identify the atomicity of the gas and write its C v.
Rearrange gamma equals one plus two over f for f. This gives f equals two over gamma minus one, the fast route straight from the ratio.
Substitute: two over one point four zero minus one, that is two over zero point four zero, which is five.
With f equal five, C v is f over two R, that is five halves R, or two point five R.
So a gas with f equal five is diatomic, and its C v is two point five R, about twenty point eight joules per mole per kelvin.
Here is the trap. A student who writes f equals two over gamma, forgetting the minus one, lands on the wrong answer. That minus one in the denominator is the whole game.

The pro move is to memorise the three benchmark values, one point six seven for monatomic, one point four zero for diatomic, one point three three for polyatomic. Then you can identify a gas by sight, with no algebra at all.
एक gas के specific heats का ratio one point four zero पाया जाता है। gas की atomicity पहचानिए और उसका C v लिखिए।
gamma बराबर one plus two over f को f के लिए rearrange कीजिए। इससे f बराबर two over gamma minus one मिलता है, ratio से सीधा तेज़ रास्ता।
substitute कीजिए: two over one point four zero minus one, यानी two over zero point four zero, जो पाँच है।
f बराबर पाँच के साथ, C v, f over two R है, यानी five halves R, या two point five R।
तो f बराबर पाँच वाली gas diatomic है, और उसका C v two point five R है, करीब twenty point eight joules per mole per kelvin।
यह रहा trap। जो student f बराबर two over gamma लिखता है, minus one भूलते हुए, गलत answer पर पहुँचता है। denominator में वह minus one ही पूरा खेल है।

pro move तीन benchmark values याद करना है, monatomic के लिए one point six seven, diatomic के लिए one point four zero, polyatomic के लिए one point three three। <whisper>फिर आप एक gas को एक नज़र में पहचान सकते हैं, बिना किसी algebra के।</whisper>

board_events.text: JEE Main example: lambda at 300 K and 1 bar
Given pressure and temperature, reach for the pressure-temperature form directly.
About 200 molecular diameters, consistent with the 'mostly free, occasionally colliding' picture.
With vav ~ 475 m/s, collision frequency nu = vav/lambda ~ 7 x 10^9 per second.

segments.text: <curious>Estimate the mean free path</curious> of a nitrogen molecule at three hundred kelvin and a pressure of one times ten to the five pascal. Take the molecular diameter as three point seven times ten to the minus ten metres and k B as one point three eight times ten to the minus twenty three.
Reach for the pressure-temperature form directly, since pressure and temperature are what the problem gives.
Lambda equals k B T over root two pi d squared P.
The numerator, k B times temperature, is one point three eight times ten to the minus twenty three, times three hundred, giving four point one four times ten to the minus twenty one joules.

The denominator uses d squared equal one point three six nine times ten to the minus nineteen: root two times pi times that times ten to the five gives about six point zero eight times ten to the minus fourteen.
Dividing, the mean free path is about six point eight times ten to the minus eight metres, roughly sixty eight nanometres.
That distance is about two hundred molecular diameters, exactly the mostly free, occasionally colliding picture of a dilute gas.

As a quick follow-on, nitrogen's average speed at this temperature is about four hundred seventy five metres per second, so the collision frequency, average speed over lambda, is about seven times ten to the nine per second. Each molecule collides roughly seven billion times every second.

एक nitrogen molecule की mean free path estimate कीजिए three hundred kelvin और one times ten to the five pascal pressure पर। molecular diameter three point seven times ten to the minus ten metres और k B one point three eight times ten to the minus twenty three लीजिए।
सीधे pressure-temperature form उठाइए, क्योंकि problem pressure और temperature ही देता है।
lambda बराबर k B T over root two pi d squared P।
numerator, k B into temperature, one point three eight times ten to the minus twenty three, into three hundred है, four point one four times ten to the minus twenty one joules देते हुए।

denominator, d squared बराबर one point three six nine times ten to the minus nineteen इस्तेमाल करता है: root two into pi into उसे into ten to the five, करीब six point zero eight times ten to the minus fourteen देता है।
divide करने पर, mean free path करीब six point eight times ten to the minus eight metres है, करीब sixty eight nanometres।
वह distance करीब दो सौ molecular diameters है, ठीक एक dilute gas की mostly free, occasionally colliding तस्वीर।

एक quick follow-on के रूप में, इस temperature पर nitrogen की average speed करीब four hundred seventy five metres per second है, तो collision frequency, average speed over lambda, करीब seven times ten to the nine per second है। <whisper>हर molecule करीब सात अरब बार हर second collide करता है।</whisper>

board_events.text: Heat capacities add by moles, because total internal energy is the sum of the parts at one temperature.
gamma ~ 1.48 sits between pure monatomic (1.67) and pure diatomic (1.40), weighted toward the more abundant oxygen.
Crucial: you cannot average gamma directly (a ratio is not additive). Average Cv, then form the ratio.

segments.text: <curious>A gas mixture</curious> is made of two moles of helium, monatomic, and three moles of oxygen, diatomic at room temperature. Find the effective gamma of the mixture.
The picture warns of the trap and the method: you average the heat capacities by moles, never the gamma values.
Heat capacities add by moles, because the total internal energy is simply the sum of the parts, sharing one temperature. So the mixture's C v is the mole-weighted average of the two.
Write the mixture's C v as n one C v one plus n two C v two, all over n one plus n two.

Helium's C v is three halves R and oxygen's is five halves R. So the numerator is two times three halves R plus three times five halves R, that is three R plus seven point five R, and dividing by five moles gives two point one R.
By Mayer's relation the mixture's C p is C v plus R, that is three point one R. So gamma is three point one R over two point one R, about one point four eight.

The mixture's gamma, about one point four eight, sits neatly between the pure monatomic value of one point six seven and the pure diatomic one point four zero, leaning toward the more abundant oxygen.

The crucial insight is that you cannot average the two gamma values directly; a ratio is not additive. Only C v is additive, through the energy, so you average C v and only then form the ratio. Averaging gamma directly gives a physically meaningless number.
एक gas mixture दो moles helium, monatomic, और तीन moles oxygen, room temperature पर diatomic, से बनी है। mixture का effective gamma निकालिए।
picture trap और method दोनों की चेतावनी देता है: आप heat capacities को moles से average करते हैं, gamma values को कभी नहीं।
heat capacities moles से add होती हैं, क्योंकि total internal energy बस भागों का जोड़ है, एक temperature share करते हुए। तो mixture का C v दोनों का mole-weighted average है।
mixture का C v लिखिए n one C v one plus n two C v two, बटा n one plus n two।

helium का C v three halves R है और oxygen का five halves R। तो numerator, two into three halves R plus three into five halves R है, यानी three R plus seven point five R, और पाँच moles से divide करने पर two point one R मिलता है।
Mayer's relation से mixture का C p, C v plus R है, यानी three point one R। तो gamma, three point one R over two point one R है, करीब one point four eight।
mixture का gamma, करीब one point four eight, pure monatomic value one point six seven और pure diatomic one point four zero के बीच अच्छे से बैठता है, ज़्यादा abundant oxygen की ओर झुकते हुए।

crucial insight यह है कि आप दोनों gamma values को सीधे average नहीं कर सकते; एक ratio additive नहीं है। सिर्फ़ C v additive है, energy के ज़रिए, तो आप C v को average करते हैं और तभी ratio बनाते हैं। <whisper>gamma को सीधे average करना एक physically meaningless number देता है।</whisper>

sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips: freedom, heat and collisions

board_events.text: The traps of a dense, high-return cluster
Diatomic: use f = 5 at room temperature, f = 7 only if 'vibration' or 'high temperature' is stated. It flips gamma between 1.40 and 1.29.
One vibration adds 2 degrees of freedom (kinetic + potential), not 1.
Molar quantities (Cv, Cp, U) use R; per-molecule energies use kB. Mixing them costs a factor of NA.
For a mixture, average Cv by moles then form gamma; never average gamma directly.
Pro-tip: memorise 1.67 / 1.40 / 1.33. Given gamma, you instantly know f, Cv and Cp; sanity-check with 'more atoms, smaller gamma'.
Memory aids: 'half a kB T to every mode', 'more atoms, smaller gamma', 'squeeze the gas, shrink the path and quicken the collisions'.

segments.text: <curious>This is a dense, high-return cluster</curious>, so the traps are worth naming precisely. Five slips and one pro-tip.

First, for diatomic gases use f equal five at room temperature, and f equal seven only when the problem explicitly invokes vibration or high temperature. Defaulting to the wrong one flips gamma between one point four zero and one point two nine.
Second, a single vibrational mode adds two degrees of freedom, not one, because it carries both kinetic and potential energy, each worth one half k B T. Adding just one is a common slip.
Third, do not swap k B and R. Molar quantities, the heat capacities and the internal energy, use R; per-molecule energies use k B. Mixing them up costs a factor of Avogadro's number, a huge error.
Fourth, for a mixture you cannot average the gamma values directly. Average C v by moles, add R for C p, and only then take the ratio, because internal energy is additive but a ratio is not.

And the pro-tip: memorise the trio one point six seven, one point four zero, one point three three for monatomic, diatomic and polyatomic. The instant a problem gives gamma you know f, C v and C p with no algebra, and you can sanity-check any answer with the rule more atoms, smaller gamma.

Finally, three phrases to lock it all in: half a k B T to every mode; more atoms, smaller gamma; and squeeze the gas, shrink the path and quicken the collisions. Those three sentences carry most of the subtopic.
यह एक dense, high-return cluster है, तो traps को ठीक-ठीक नाम देना फ़ायदेमंद है। पाँच slips और एक pro-tip।

पहला, diatomic gases के लिए room temperature पर f बराबर पाँच इस्तेमाल कीजिए, और f बराबर सात सिर्फ़ तब जब problem explicitly vibration या high temperature invoke करे। गलत वाला default करना gamma को one point four zero और one point two nine के बीच पलट देता है।
दूसरा, एक single vibrational mode दो degrees of freedom जोड़ता है, एक नहीं, क्योंकि यह kinetic और potential energy दोनों रखता है, हर एक one half k B T की। सिर्फ़ एक जोड़ना एक common slip है।

तीसरा, k B और R को मत बदलिए। molar quantities, heat capacities और internal energy, R इस्तेमाल करते हैं; per-molecule energies k B इस्तेमाल करते हैं। इन्हें मिलाना Avogadro number का factor खर्च कराता है, एक भारी error।
चौथा, एक mixture के लिए आप gamma values को सीधे average नहीं कर सकते। C v को moles से average कीजिए, C p के लिए R जोड़िए, और तभी ratio लीजिए, क्योंकि internal energy additive है पर एक ratio नहीं।

और pro-tip: monatomic, diatomic और polyatomic के लिए तिकड़ी one point six seven, one point four zero, one point three three याद कीजिए। जैसे ही problem gamma देता है आपको बिना algebra के f, C v और C p पता हैं, और आप किसी भी answer को rule more atoms, smaller gamma से sanity-check कर सकते हैं।

आख़िर में, तीन वाक्य सब कुछ पक्का करने के लिए: हर mode को आधा k B T; more atoms, smaller gamma; और gas को squeeze कीजिए, path को shrink कीजिए और collisions को तेज़ कीजिए। <whisper>वे तीन वाक्य इस subtopic का ज़्यादातर हिस्सा ढो लेते हैं।</whisper>

sections.title: The golden thread and master formula sheet

board_events.text: One idea, unfolded into the whole chapter
Far-apart molecules obey PV = nRT; kinetic theory explains why; temperature turns out to be energy; degrees of freedom turn it into heat capacities.

board_events.latex: PV = nRT = Nk_BT \;\xrightarrow{\text{kinetic theory}}\; P = \tfrac{1}{3}\rho v_{rms}^2,\; PV = \tfrac{2}{3}E
PV=nRT=\tfrac{m}{M}RT=Nk_BT;\quad P=\tfrac{\rho RT}{M};\quad P=\tfrac{1}{3}\tfrac{N}{V}m\langle v^2\rangle;\quad PV=\tfrac{2}{3}E

segments.text: <curious>Before we finish</curious>, let us see the whole chapter as one connected chain. Everything grows from a single seed: matter is made of countless tiny molecules in ceaseless, random motion.

Because molecules are far apart, gases behave simply, and their behaviour collapses into one master relation, pressure times volume equals n R T. Kinetic theory then explains why that law holds, and comparing it with the molecular form reveals the meaning of temperature. Finally, counting the ways a molecule stores energy turns temperature into internal energy and specific heats.

Here is the golden thread, worth memorising. From pressure times volume equals n R T, equal to N k B T, kinetic theory gives pressure equals one third rho v r m s squared, and pressure times volume equals two thirds of the energy.

Setting the kinetic pressure equal to N k B T gives one half m mean square speed equals three halves k B T, the kinetic meaning of temperature, from which the r m s speed follows as the root of three R T over M.

And equipartition closes the chain: the internal energy is f over two n R T, giving C v as f over two R, C p as C v plus R, and gamma as one plus two over f. Reproduce this chain and you can re-derive almost every formula in the chapter on demand.

Now the master sheet, gathered in one place. The gas laws and ideal gas equation in all their forms, with the density form pressure equals rho R T over M; and the kinetic pressure, one third number density m mean square speed, equal to two thirds the energy density.

The three speeds keep their fixed ratio, root three to root eight over pi to root two, r m s largest. And the degree-of-freedom results give the internal energy and the specific heats, with f three, five, six for monatomic, diatomic and non-linear polyatomic.

And the mean free path, one over root two pi d squared n, with the collision frequency v average over lambda. Two unit rules underpin all of it: temperature always in kelvin, and molar mass in kilograms per mole inside the speed formulas.
ख़त्म करने से पहले, चलिए पूरे chapter को एक connected chain के रूप में देखें। सब कुछ एक ही बीज से बढ़ता है: matter अनगिनत tiny molecules से बना है जो ceaseless, random motion में हैं।

क्योंकि molecules दूर-दूर हैं, gases simply behave करती हैं, और उनका behaviour एक master relation में सिमट जाता है, pressure into volume बराबर n R T। kinetic theory फिर समझाती है कि वह law क्यों valid है, और उसे molecular form से compare करने पर temperature का मतलब खुलता है। आख़िर में, एक molecule energy स्टोर करने के तरीके गिनना temperature को internal energy और specific heats में बदल देता है।

यह रही golden thread, याद करने लायक़। pressure into volume बराबर n R T, बराबर N k B T से, kinetic theory देती है pressure बराबर one third rho v r m s squared, और pressure into volume बराबर energy का two thirds।

kinetic pressure को N k B T के बराबर रखने पर one half m mean square speed बराबर three halves k B T मिलता है, temperature का kinetic meaning, जिससे r m s speed three R T over M के root के रूप में निकलती है।

और equipartition chain को बंद करती है: internal energy f over two n R T है, C v को f over two R देते हुए, C p को C v plus R, और gamma को one plus two over f। इस chain को दोहराइए और आप chapter की लगभग हर formula demand पर फिर से derive कर सकते हैं।

अब master sheet, एक जगह इकट्ठी। gas laws और ideal gas equation अपने सारे रूपों में, density form pressure बराबर rho R T over M के साथ; और kinetic pressure, one third number density m mean square speed, energy density के two thirds के बराबर।

तीन speeds अपना fixed ratio रखती हैं, root three to root eight over pi to root two, r m s सबसे बड़ी। और degree-of-freedom results internal energy और specific heats देते हैं, monatomic, diatomic और non-linear polyatomic के लिए f तीन, पाँच, छह के साथ।

और mean free path, one over root two pi d squared n, collision frequency v average over lambda के साथ। <whisper>दो unit rules इस सबके नीचे हैं: temperature हमेशा kelvin में, और speed formulas के अंदर molar mass kilograms per mole में।</whisper>

sections.title: Whole-chapter cheat sheet

board_events.text: The entire chapter in quick-recall boxes
Molecular nature: matter is molecules in motion. Molecular size ~1 angstrom; gas spacing ~10x; mean free path ~100x the spacing. A gas is ~99.96% empty.
Gas laws: PV = nRT = (m/M)RT = NkBT; P = rho RT/M. Boyle (T fixed), Charles (P fixed); Dalton adds partial pressures; Graham rate proportional to 1/sqrt(M).
Kinetic pressure: P = (1/3) rho vrms^2 = (1/3)(N/V) m mean-square; PV = (2/3)E; E = (3/2)PV. The 1/3 is the isotropy factor.
Temperature is energy: (1/2)m mean-square = (3/2)kBT. Speeds vrms = sqrt(3RT/M), vav = sqrt(8RT/piM), vmp = sqrt(2RT/M); order RAM. Read the Maxwell curve as area.
Freedom & heat: (1/2)kBT per mode; U = (f/2)nRT; Cv = (f/2)R, Cp = Cv+R, gamma = 1+2/f. Benchmarks 1.67 / 1.40 / 1.33 for mono / di / poly.
Mean free path: lambda = 1/(root2 pi d^2 n) = kBT/(root2 pi d^2 P); lambda proportional to T/P. Collision frequency nu = vav/lambda. Dulong-Petit solid 3R; water 9R.
Never forget: kelvin + kg/mol; P proportional to vrms^2 not vrms; T is energy; order RAM; gamma identifies the gas; lambda proportional to T/P.
One seed: molecules in motion. If you can rebuild the golden thread, the whole chapter is yours.

segments.text: <excited>Here is the entire chapter</excited> distilled into quick-recall boxes, one per subtopic. Read this last, the night before the exam.

Sub-topic zero, the molecular nature of matter. All matter is molecules in perpetual motion. Carry three scales: molecular size about one angstrom, gas spacing about ten times that, and the mean free path about a hundred times the spacing. A gas is overwhelmingly empty space.

Sub-topic one, the gas laws. One master relation, pressure times volume equals n R T, equal to mass over molar mass R T, equal to N k B T, with the density form pressure equals rho R T over M. Boyle holds at fixed temperature, Charles at fixed pressure; Dalton adds partial pressures; Graham makes the diffusion rate go as one over root molar mass.

Sub-topic two, kinetic theory and pressure. Pressure is one third rho v r m s squared, equal to one third number density m mean square speed, and pressure times volume is two thirds of the total kinetic energy. That factor of one third is the fingerprint of three-dimensional isotropy.

Sub-topic three, r m s speed and the Maxwell distribution. Temperature is average kinetic energy: one half m mean square speed equals three halves k B T. The three speeds are root three, root eight over pi, and root two times R T over M, in the fixed order r m s, average, most probable. Read the Maxwell curve as an area, never a height.

Sub-topic four, degrees of freedom and equipartition. Each mode carries one half k B T, so the internal energy is f over two n R T, giving C v as f over two R, C p as C v plus R, and gamma as one plus two over f. Memorise the benchmark gammas, one point six seven, one point four zero, one point three three, for monatomic, diatomic and polyatomic.

Still sub-topic four, the mean free path is one over root two pi d squared n, equal to k B T over root two pi d squared P, so lambda goes as temperature over pressure. The collision frequency is the average speed over lambda. And equipartition reaches solids too: Dulong and Petit give three R, and water nine R.

Six things to never forget. Temperature in kelvin and molar mass in kilograms per mole. Pressure goes as the square of the r m s speed, never the speed itself. Temperature is energy, the same for every gas at a given temperature. The order is r m s, average, most probable. Gamma identifies the gas. And the mean free path goes as temperature over pressure.
And the one seed the whole chapter grows from: molecules in ceaseless motion. If you can rebuild the golden thread from that single idea, the entire chapter is yours.
यह रहा पूरा chapter quick-recall boxes में distilled, हर subtopic का एक। इसे आख़िर में पढ़िए, exam से एक रात पहले।

sub-topic zero, matter की molecular nature। सारा matter perpetual motion में molecules है। तीन scales रखिए: molecular size करीब एक angstrom, gas spacing उसका करीब दस गुना, और mean free path spacing का करीब सौ गुना। एक gas बड़े पैमाने पर खाली जगह है।

sub-topic one, gas laws। एक master relation, pressure into volume बराबर n R T, बराबर mass over molar mass R T, बराबर N k B T, density form pressure बराबर rho R T over M के साथ। Boyle fixed temperature पर valid है, Charles fixed pressure पर; Dalton partial pressures जोड़ता है; Graham diffusion rate को one over root molar mass के जैसे बनाता है।

sub-topic two, kinetic theory और pressure। pressure one third rho v r m s squared है, बराबर one third number density m mean square speed, और pressure into volume total kinetic energy का two thirds है। one third का वह factor three-dimensional isotropy का fingerprint है।

sub-topic three, r m s speed और Maxwell distribution। temperature average kinetic energy है: one half m mean square speed बराबर three halves k B T। तीन speeds root three, root eight over pi, और root two into R T over M हैं, fixed order r m s, average, most probable में। Maxwell curve को एक area की तरह पढ़िए, कभी height की तरह नहीं।

sub-topic four, degrees of freedom और equipartition। हर mode one half k B T रखता है, तो internal energy f over two n R T है, C v को f over two R देते हुए, C p को C v plus R, और gamma को one plus two over f। benchmark gammas याद कीजिए, monatomic, diatomic और polyatomic के लिए one point six seven, one point four zero, one point three three।

अब भी sub-topic four, mean free path one over root two pi d squared n है, बराबर k B T over root two pi d squared P, तो lambda temperature over pressure के जैसे चलता है। collision frequency average speed over lambda है। और equipartition solids तक पहुँचती है: Dulong और Petit तीन R देते हैं, और water nine R।

छह चीज़ें कभी मत भूलिए। temperature kelvin में और molar mass kilograms per mole में। pressure r m s speed के square के जैसे चलता है, कभी speed के जैसे नहीं। temperature energy है, दिए गए temperature पर हर gas के लिए एक जैसी। order r m s, average, most probable है। gamma gas को पहचानता है। और mean free path temperature over pressure के जैसे चलता है।
और वह एक बीज जिससे पूरा chapter बढ़ता है: ceaseless motion में molecules। <whisper>अगर आप उस एक idea से golden thread दोबारा बना सकते हैं, पूरा chapter आपका है।</whisper>
